cards.text: Jesus has been teaching the crowds about reading the times (Luke 12:54-56). Then some people standing there tell Him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate, the governor of Judea (Luke 3:1), had mixed with their sacrifices.

cards.question: Jesus hears about the Galileans whose blood Pilate mixed with their sacrifices. What does He ask the crowd about them?

answers.text: Were they worse sinners than other Galileans
Did they offer the wrong kind of sacrifices
Why did nobody try to stop Pilate

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd that those Galileans really were worse sinners than all the other Galileans.

cards.text: Jesus says no, they weren't, and then He turns it right back on the crowd. I know that feeling, friend: I bring up something I heard, and two seconds later everybody's looking at ME.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd that unless they ___, they too will all perish.

cards.text: Then Jesus brings up the eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them. He asks the crowd if they were more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem.

cards.question: Jesus gives the crowd the same warning about the eighteen killed by the tower of Siloam that He gave about the Galileans.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish." That's the warning He gave about the Galileans, word for word.
Then Jesus tells a parable. A man has a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he goes looking for fruit on it.

cards.question: The man goes to his fig tree looking for fruit. What does he find?

cards.text: He tells the keeper of the vineyard that for the past three years he's come searching this tree for fruit, and still nothing. I've done that with an oven: open it, close it, open it again, STILL nothing.

cards.question: After three years with no fruit, what does the owner tell the keeper of the vineyard to do with the fig tree?

cards.text: The owner even asks, "Why should it use up the soil?" Oof. I felt that one, friend, the day Mother Miller brought home a shiny new stamper and slid me into the junk drawer.

cards.question: The owner wants the fig tree cut down. But the keeper of the vineyard asks him to leave it alone one more ___.
The keeper of the vineyard wants the fig tree left alone one more year. What does he plan to do for it in that time?

answers.text: Dig around it and fertilize it
Prune its branches and water it
Build a fence all around it

cards.question: The keeper of the vineyard promises the owner that the fig tree will bear fruit next year.

cards.text: No promises, friend. The keeper says if it bears fruit next year, fine, but if not, the owner can cut it down.
